sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **CBDR-RC**: India advocates for 'Common But Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities', emphasizing historical emissions of developed nations.
• **Panchamrit Strategy**: India's 5-point climate agenda announced at COP26 (Glasgow) including Net Zero by 2070.
• **NAPCC**: The National Action Plan on Climate Change (2008) serves as the umbrella policy framework with 8 National Missions.
• **Key Metric**: India's per capita emissions are significantly lower than the global average, yet it is highly vulnerable to climate-induced extreme weather events.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **National Missions**: 8 missions including Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, and Himalayan Ecosystem.
• **LiFE Movement**: 'Lifestyle for Environment' promoting sustainable consumption patterns to combat climate change.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Balancing coal dependency for energy security vs. green transition; climate finance gaps.
• **Solutions**: Climate-resilient infrastructure, carbon pricing mechanisms, and technology transfer.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'S-H-A-W-S-A-M-S' (8 Missions of NAPCC).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Solar, Habitat, Agriculture, Water, Sustainable Himalayan, Energy Efficiency, Mission on Strategic Knowledge, Mission on Green India.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Net Zero' (2070) with 'Carbon Neutrality' or specific sectoral targets. Always verify the target year.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Climate Justice' to describe India's stance in international negotiations.

keyTakeaways: India's climate policy is rooted in equity and development needs.
The NAPCC is the foundational policy document, but it is supplemented by newer initiatives like the Green Hydrogen Mission.
India is a global leader in climate action through initiatives like ISA and CDRI.
